title: Quota cursor hunting — adhoc debug notes
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Sporadic 429 spikes for a small set of clients between 09:12-09:20 UTC on Feb 13. Not global; appears tied to specific API keys (same keys seen across multiple app instances). 401s rare but seen close to rotation times.
- Goal: find root cause (windowing, client-side burst, auth proxy bug, clock skew, stale routing). Build minimal repro and capture breadcrumbs.

What I saw (raw) — snippets from logs and quick curl output:
- Example 429 response (header details captured):
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Content-Type: application/json
  Retry-After: 11
  Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2024 09:14:07 GMT
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset: 1707794047
  {"error":"quota_exceeded","detail":"per-minute token limit reached"}

- Example 401 during key rotation window:
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2024 09:15:42 GMT
  WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=\"redwood\", error=\"invalid_token\"
  {"error":"invalid_api_key","msg":"key not found"}

Hypotheses (ranked, quick):
1) Quota cursor drift: auth-service maintains per-key cursor with minute buckets; under high concurrency cursor increment race causes incorrectly computed remaining (clients see Remaining=0 prematurely).
2) Client burst misreporting: client library retries without reading Retry-After header, spinning requests and exhausting shared per-key budget.
3) Upstream caching / proxy (edge) serving stale X-RateLimit headers. Edge caches / headers for the wrong key when cache key not granular enough.
4) Key rotation race: new key not propagated to all auth nodes quickly -> short 401 followed by flood as clients reattempt with backoff disabled.
5) Clock skew on a single auth node causing X-RateLimit-Reset values to be a few seconds off leading to early rejects.

Commands I ran (repro + capture):
- Basic diagnostic curl (captures headers + body):
  KEY=sk_live_test123
  curl -s -D - -o /tmp/resp.json -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

- Verbose TLS + headers to inspect connection reuse:
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 2>&1 | tee curl-verbose.log

- Loop to saturate per-minute windows (local repro):
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health & done; wait
  # watch for 429 flood, check headers on first 429 responses

- Capture TCP-level ordering (when I suspected proxy):
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap port 443 and host api.redwood.ai &
  (then run short burst)

- Compare two keys side-by-side (one that hits 429, one that doesn't):
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_problem" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_control" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

Observations from experiments:
- Header patterns consistent: X-RateLimit-Remaining toggles to 0 repeatedly in short intervals (not monotonically decreasing then reset). That suggests a per-minute cursor issue (or mis-aggregation across shards).
- When two app instances use the same key, the bursts align with deploys / cold starts. One instance appears to send a group of queued requests at startup.
- In the pcap, I saw several requests identical in sequence numbers arriving within sub-ms — points to client-side retry storm or nginx connection reuse issues.
- 401s coincide with our key-rotation lambda events (we refresh ephemeral keys every 24h). The 401s last ~3–8s before the auth cache repopulates.

Quick reproducer steps I left in the sandbox:
- Use test key 'sk_test_cursor' on staging. Run this script (bash):
  1) baseline: curl -i once and record headers.
  2) parallel flood: for i in $(seq 1 120); do curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_cursor" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/health & done; wait
  3) capture first 429 and note X-RateLimit-Reset timestamp and convert to human time: date -u -d @<reset>
  4) repeat with two separate hosts (or two containers) to simulate app fleet.

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- Don't trust only X-RateLimit-Remaining; look at server-side counters in DB and auth-service logs. Headers can be stale if a proxy cache exists.
- If Retry-After present, enforce client-side honor at SDK-level. Many clients ignore it today.
- For rotation-induced 401s, add ephemeral-key warm-up where rotate -> push to auth-cache -> then switch clients. Avoid switch-before-cache.

Things to check next (action items):
- [ ] Add instrumentation to auth-service: emit per-key cursor value changes + shard-id + leader-election marker. Correlate with timestamp when Remaining jumps to 0. (owner: @Sofia)
- [ ] Confirm whether edge cache (CDN/nginx) has caching on Authorization or other header that could cause header mixing. Check confs. (owner: @Leo)
- [ ] Run coordinated experiment with two containers, each with different request patterns (one steady, one bursty) using same key to see how remaining is consumed. Capture both sides. (me)
- [ ] Add short experiment to disable connection reuse for a client and see if retry storms vanish (curl --no-keepalive).
- [ ] Look at recent deploys to auth and edge around Feb 13 09:00-09:30. Any config flips? (ops)

Tentative mitigations (fast):
- Server: Add jittered per-key request acceptance to smooth sudden group arrivals (drop some at random instead of full-0).
- SDK: Honor Retry-After and exponential backoff by default; set a client-wide circuit-breaker for 429s.
- Rotation: introduce a rolling-warm cache propagation step so clients don't flip keys until caches ack the new key.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does X-RateLimit-Remaining increase back from 0 to >0 before reset? Is aggregation across multiple auth nodes mixing counters?
- Are there any intermediate proxies doing transparent buffering of requests that release them in bursts? (old haproxy misconfig?)
- How correlated are these events with specific customer patterns (cron-jobs, warmup traffic)? Need to map clients by fingerprint.

Log snippets to keep (for later paste into ticket):
- 2024-02-13T09:14:07Z auth-01 INFO cursor_increment key=sk_live_problem shard=3 prev=599 new=0 ttl=60
- 2024-02-13T09:15:42Z auth-02 WARN cache_miss key=sk_live_problem reason=stale-ttl
- app-12 ERROR client-retry storm: 91 concurrent retries after 401

Final quick notes:
- This is messy, but pattern leans toward cursor/shard aggregation bug + client retry amplification.
- Prioritize auth-service instrumentation + small SDK change (honor Retry-After) as quickest wins.

TODO later (brain dump):
- Build small simulator to emulate 1000 clients with shared key and see counter behavior under different shard strategies.
- Audit all places that mutate per-key counters for atomicity (redis scripts? db transactions?).
- Check if any CDNs are set to cache Authorization headers incorrectly (edge config audit).

----
Scratchpad ends. Will sync with Sofia/Leo after they push the instrumentation PRs.
